dialogue:
A: So, have you been keeping up with the World Baseball Classic? 

B: Oh, absolutely! I mean, it’s hard not to with all the excitement going on. What about you? Did you catch the game with Chinese Taipei?

A: I did! What a nail-biter, right? They managed to edge out Korea 5-4 in ten innings. I was on the edge of my seat!

B: Seriously! That game had everything. Ruei-Yang Gu Lin pitched a solid game, and the crowd in Tokyo was electric. 

A: Right? And that solo homer by Yu Chang in the second inning? That place erupted! 

B: I know, I mean, who doesn’t love a good home run? But then Korea tied it up, and I was thinking, “Oh no, not like this!” 

A: Exactly! Just when you think Chinese Taipei has it in the bag, Korea comes back and takes the lead. But then—bam!—Stuart Fairchild hits that two-run homer in the eighth. 

B: Talk about drama! I was like, “Is this a movie?” It’s wild how the momentum shifts in these games. 

A: Totally! And now, with Chinese Taipei’s win, they’re just waiting to see if they can advance. They must be biting their nails watching Australia play Japan. 

B: Right? It’s like they’re on a rollercoaster of emotions. They could still sneak into the quarterfinals, but it’s a bit of a nail-biter scenario. 

A: I love how unpredictable the WBC is. Unlike, you know, some leagues where it feels like the same teams dominate every year. 

B: Yeah, it really keeps you guessing. And I mean, the talent pool is just so diverse. You've got teams from all over the world, and they all want that title.

A: Exactly! And did you see the standings for Pool C? Japan clinched a spot in the quarterfinals already. They’re looking strong this year.

B: For sure! Japan is always a powerhouse in international baseball. But man, I really want to see Chinese Taipei make a deep run. It’d be such a great story.

A: Agreed! And can you imagine the celebrations if they do? The streets of Taipei would be packed!

B: Oh, for sure! I mean, we should probably book our tickets just in case, right? 

A: Ha! Let’s do it! But first, we should see how Korea fares against Australia. 

B: Definitely! I’ll be glued to the screen. I can't wait to see how it all unfolds!

SOURCE TITLE: 2026 World Baseball Classic: Chinese Taipei Defeats Korea 5-4 in ...
SOURCE CONTENT: Chinese Taipei threw a wrench into Pool C of the World Baseball Classic on Sunday afternoon, edging Korea 5-4 in ten innings behind a strong start from Ruei-Yang Gu Lin and timely hitting.
Following two shutout losses to open the tournament, Chinese Taipei rebounded with two crucial wins and must await the results of Australia vs. Japan and Australia vs. Korea to determine whether they can advance to the quarterfinals via a second-place tiebreaker.
With Chinese Taipei’s win, Japan officially clinched a spot in the quarterfinals. Korea will face Australia tomorrow night. Australia controls its own destiny, but if it loses to Japan tonight, Korea’s hopes will remain alive. In that case, Korea would need a win to potentially advance through a tiebreaker.
Yu Chang opened the scoring with a solo home run off Hyun Jin Ryu in the second inning, igniting the packed Taiwanese crowd at the Tokyo Dome.
Korea chased Gu Lin from the game in the fifth and tied it when Shay Whitcomb bounced into a double play that brought home Hyun Min Ahn.
Tsung-Che Cheng put Chinese Taipei back in front in the sixth with a solo shot, but Do Yeong Kim answered with a towering two-run home run to left field off Wei-En Lin to give Korea its first lead of the day.
Gu Lin pitched admirably for Chinese Taipei, allowing just two hits and one run while working into the fifth inning on 59 pitches. Lin then added 2 ⅓ innings in relief, striking out four while allowing two runs.
Ryu went three innings for Korea, throwing 50 pitches and allowing one run on three hits with three strikeouts. Gwak Been followed with 3 ⅓ innings, giving up one run on two hits while striking out three.
In the seventh, Chinese Taipei put the tying run on second and the go-ahead run on first, but Dane Dunning entered and immediately induced a double play to end the threat.
With two outs in the eighth, the game flipped again when Stuart Fairchild hit an opposite-field two-run homer off Dunning to give Chinese Taipei a 4-3 lead.
